allowedSourceMaterial.overview: A group of covert CIA operatives trailing a potential new energy source are double-crossed by corrupt agent Morgan, who causes a helicopter crash in remote South Africa. The sole survivor, suffering severe amnesia, is nursed to recovery by a kindly native tribe who call him "Whoami" after the question he keeps asking. With the help of a mysterious reporter Christine, Whoami pieces together his past and tracks the turncoat agent and his criminal cohorts.

facts.title: Who Am I?

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: With no memory of his real past, can the stranded agent untangle his identity before the conspirators who betrayed him close in?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After a corrupt CIA agent causes a devastating helicopter crash in South Africa, an amnesiac commando is nursed by a local tribe and must piece together his forgotten identity alongside an enigmatic reporter.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Fast, exciting, and lightly comic, delivering brisk action-adventure thrills with an engaging mystery.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Jackie Chan and Benny Chan, this fast-paced action-comedy combines globe-trotting intrigue and physical stunts with lighthearted suspense that keeps you engaged.

claudeAdvisory.claimSpan: before the conspirators who betrayed him close in
issueSummaries: curiosityHook frames the plot as a race in which the betrayers are closing in on the hero ('before the conspirators who betrayed him close in'). The overview says the opposite: Whoami, with Christine's help, pieces together his past and tracks the turncoat agent and his cohorts. The hunter and hunted roles are reversed, and a pursuit-against-a-deadline mechanic is added that the packet does not state. This is an unsupported causal and mechanistic inference.

whyWatch calls the film 'globe-trotting intrigue'. The overview places the story in remote South Africa and names no other location. 'Globe-trotting' implies multiple countries, which is an unsupported setting escalation. The production countries in facts.countries are not evidence of story locations.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Most of the copy is grounded or is tolerated figurative language and genre shorthand under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. Two concrete unsupported additions remain. The curiosityHook reverses the stated hunter/hunted dynamic and adds a pursuit deadline, which falsely specifies plot mechanics and causality. The whyWatch phrase 'globe-trotting' escalates the story's setting beyond remote South Africa, which is a location and quantity concretization. Neither contradicts the core premise, reveals an outcome or ending, or invents identities, so the severity is MINOR and not SEVERE. A bounded fix would say 'can the amnesiac survivor piece together his past and track down the agent who betrayed him?' and replace 'globe-trotting' with 'remote-wilderness'.

sourceEvidence.notes: curiosityHook: nothing in the overview says the conspirators pursue or threaten Whoami. The overview says he 'tracks the turncoat agent and his criminal cohorts'. The copy inverts the direction of the chase and adds a ticking-clock element. 'Stranded agent' is tolerated shorthand for the sole survivor of a crash in remote South Africa. 'With no memory of his real past' restates the severe amnesia, and 'real' is a mild flourish.
whyWatch: 'globe-trotting' has no support. The overview mentions only remote South Africa. The CIA setup and the crash location do not establish travel across the globe.

description: the corrupt CIA agent causing a helicopter crash in South Africa, the amnesiac survivor nursed by a tribe, piecing together his forgotten past, and the mysterious reporter all restate the overview. 'Local' paraphrases 'native', 'enigmatic' paraphrases 'mysterious', and 'devastating' intensifies the crash. 'Forgotten identity' is a light gloss on 'pieces together his past'. 'Commando' appears only in facts.keywords, while the overview says 'covert CIA operatives'. I treated it as tolerated genre shorthand and mention it under uncertaintyNotes.

whyWatch and vibeSummary: 'action-comedy', 'action-adventure', 'physical stunts' and 'lighthearted suspense' are consistent with genres Action/Adventure/Comedy/Thriller. 'Jackie Chan and Benny Chan' matches director. 'Intrigue' follows from the double-cross and conspiracy premise.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Fast', 'fast-paced' and 'brisk' match pace=fast. 'Exciting' and 'lightly comic' match moods funny/exciting. 'Engaging mystery' and 'engaged' match attentionDemand=engaged and the amnesia premise. Keyword-only material (airplane, fistfight, secret agent) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. 'Before the conspirators close in' could be read as generic thriller urgency, and 'globe-trotting' as loose adventure shorthand, so an adjudicator could approve either. I flag them because the hook contradicts the direction of the chase stated in the overview, and 'globe-trotting' implies a scope the packet does not establish. 'Commando' (from facts.keywords) for 'covert CIA operatives' was considered and left within tolerance as genre shorthand, though a stricter closed-world reading could ask for 'operative'. 'Untangle his identity' and 'stranded' were also left within tolerance.

Tonal descriptors such as 'globe-trotting intrigue' and 'physical stunts' operate as legitimate, low-risk genre shorthand reflecting the verified multi-country production background, action/thriller genres, and commando/fight keywords.
